summary: 1921 cupola cabin on Copper Butte, Ferry County, WA; removed or destroyed in the 1950s. A 2024 hike write-up says only a rusted bed frame and debris remain.

facts.design: Cupola cabin built 1921; a 1925 USGS note describes a 12-by-12 house topped by a 6-foot cupola on the summit

staffing.status: three lookouts named: Ray Ward (1923), Harold White (1929), Lee Roy Kinnan (1945); no later staffing in the sources read

access.note: Open hiking access on Colville National Forest land by the Old Stagecoach Trail and Kettle Crest trail, per WTA and Hike of the Week. Check for current trail notices.

visit.trail_note: About 3 miles along the route to the summit, a 6-mile round trip per Hike of the Week. No tower remains to climb.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites register and WillhiteWeb say the cupola was removed in the 1950s; the Fire Lookout page says the cabin was destroyed in that decade. No source gives a date or method, so the story reports both words.

notes_for_editor: The Spokesman-Review and Republic News-Miner passages reach us through WillhiteWeb and a Weebly transcription; the newspapers themselves were not read. Staffing names come from one source (Fire Lookout). The hike write-up is from June 2024, so today's condition is two years old. The Former Fire Lookout Sites registration date was not visible on the cached page and is not used. The 1950s removed-versus-destroyed question is unresolved.
